By Wesley Yin-Poole Updated : Nov 10, 2026 3:49pm UTC Add IGN on Google 0 5 Rockstar has released a new GTA 6 trailer announcing the launch of preloads, and it includes new footage. Preloading is now available for everyone who has preordered GTA 6 digitally (those who preordered the code-in-the-box version can also activate their code and begin preloading as soon as it’s received). Rockstar has also, finally, announced the performance specifications GTA 6 is shooting for across PlayStation 5, PlayStation 5 Pro, Xbox Series X and S, and even Xbox One, but our focus here is the accompanying new trailer. While it’s only 29 seconds long, it does include snippets of never-before-seen footage, which has already got fans talking. The trailer, which features ‘Blood in Your Eyes’ by Tove Lo from Grand Theft Auto VI: The Album, starts with the “Plays Best on PS5” message we’ve seen on pretty much all the GTA 6 marketing material so far, per Sony’s partnership with Rockstar Games. We then see Lucia and Jason dancing together in a nightclub, before we switch to a racetrack in the daytime, where Lucia watches an enthusiastic driver do a backflip. We then switch to a character saying, “I mean, it’s not really my thing, you know what I’m sayin’?” This is music producer Dre'Quan Priest (“Now that he's signed the Real Dimez, Dre'Quan's days of booking acts into Boobie's strip club might be numbered as he sets his sights on the Vice City scene.”) We then see Jason push someone into a shower (I think it’s a shower!), a party on a boat called “Ships And Giggles,” and then something interesting: a SWAT team that looks like it’s responding to an emergency of some sort. My best guess is these guys are part of the team that assaulted the building Jason and Lucia escape from in the Extended Look. GTA 6 Launch Screenshots View 39 Images We then see Lucia and a friend getting ready for a night out, before another character makes a dramatic exit, saying, “Oh, it is so on now!” GTA 6 launches on November 19, and we’ve got the global release times so you know when you can start playing . This week, IGN interviewed Take-Two boss Strauss Zelnick to talk GTA 6 expectations , Online, and what the next decade looks like.
